author: markdboyd
body:
## Changes proposed in this pull request:

Closes https://github.com/cloud-gov/aws-broker/issues/386
Closes https://github.com/cloud-gov/aws-broker/issues/303

This PR adds support for enabling RDS read replicas, including:

- New broker plans for creating databases without read replicas, e.g. `micro-psql-replica`
- Logic to manage RDS read replicas:
  - Create them when creating a service, if necessary
  - Create them when modifying a service's plan, if necessary
  - Delete them when deleting a service, if necessary
- Updating the RDS create, modify, and delete handlers to use async jobs
- Updating the RDS last operation handler to fetch the async job status in the database for create, modify, and delete operations
 - Adding `AsyncJobMsg` as a database model for storing the status of async jobs initiated by the broker 

There are non-functional changes included in this PR as well:

- Refactoring code for better testability and avoiding test code mixed with production code
- Deleting unused code

## Things to check

- For any logging statements, is there any chance that they could be logging sensitive data?
- Are log statements using a logging library with a logging level set? Setting a logging level means that log statements "below" that level will not be written to the output. For example, if the logging level is set to `INFO` and debugging statements are written with `log.debug` or similar, then they won't be written to the otput, which can prevent unintentional leaks of sensitive data.

## Security considerations

The code changes are not sensitive. Adding support for read replicas on brokered databases has no additional security risk that I can think of, since it is just a read-only copy of the primary database.

This change permits a cache per version of a resource by setting the filename to the resources_id + resource_version.

body:
This PR introduces the ability for consumers of the `genesys-cloud-client-auth` library to inject custom HTTP headers (such as `Genesys-App`) into all API requests made by the authenticator, including internal requests like token validation.

### Details

- **Configuration Update:**  
  The `IAuthenticatorConfig` interface now supports an optional `customHeaders` property, allowing consumers to specify a map of headers to include with every API request.

- **Implementation:**  
  - The `GenesysCloudClientAuthenticator` class stores and applies these custom headers to all outgoing HTTP requests, ensuring they are present for both user-initiated and internal requests.
  - The `callApi` method was updated to merge and send the custom headers with each request.

- **Documentation:**  
  The README.md has been updated to document the new `customHeaders` option, including usage examples and configuration details.

### Motivation

This enhancement enables integrators to meet organizational or platform requirements for custom headers (e.g., for tracking, analytics, or compliance) without modifying the library’s internals.

author: scottrhoyt
body:
# Issue/Motivation

SwiftSyntax 601.0.1 is the first version of the library that supports the [new preview for prebuilts in SPM](https://forums.swift.org/t/preview-swift-syntax-prebuilts-for-macros/80202). This functionality dramatically improves build times (especially in release configuration) for macro libraries. Now that Mockable 0.4.0 [supports SwiftSyntax v601](https://github.com/Kolos65/Mockable/pull/120), the path is cleared for this library.

## Tasklist

- [x] Update `Package.swift` to support SwiftSyntax up to and including v601.
- [x] Add conditional support for new generic argument API in SwiftSyntax v601.
- [x] Build `MapLibreSwiftUI` in debug/release configurations and benchmark against SwiftSyntax 510.0.3 and 601.0.1.

## Outcome

`MapLibreSwiftUI` builds dramatically faster in both configurations. While it was hard to benchmark builds in Xcode accurately--since `swift build` will fail--I saw times drop from several minutes to archive down to just a matter of seconds. This is consistent with the results I saw on `Mockable` with release builds falling from ~140s down to 9s.

> [!CAUTION]
> `MapLibreSwiftUI` won't build against SwiftSyntax 601.0.0 due to a missing marker module that was [fixed in 601.0.1](https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-syntax/pull/3036).

### Steps to reproduce:

- Create a storable product P with 10 units in stock.
- Inventory > Configuration > Warehouse Management > Operation Types
- Change the reservation Method of Delivery orders to Manual
- Create confirm and manually assign a delivery order for 3 units of P
- Process the DO in the barcode app, scan 1 unit of P
> The line should be 1/3
- Leave and come back
#### > The line is now at 1/1

Cause of the issue:

Leaving the barcode app launch a call of the `split_uncompleted_moves` in order to keep track of the initial reservation in the barcode app: https://github.com/odoo/enterprise/blob/577cb4b74a614d2dd472375b325706525ae591d7/stock_barcode/models/stock_move.py#L9-L11 
However, one of the issue of the current system is that these new moves are expected to be assigned by the `_action_confirm`: https://github.com/odoo/enterprise/blob/577cb4b74a614d2dd472375b325706525ae591d7/stock_barcode/models/stock_move.py#L37
But they are not in certain cases and we should therefore force re-assignation in that case:
https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/bf0461552effe806fdaa8f85f088be3c3f3be09d/addons/stock/models/stock_move.py#L1427-L1432

### Summary

This PR updates the project to be able to use the new value `ibm_quantum_platform` from Qiskit Runtime 0.40.0 version.

### Details and comments

- Support in the client:

The functionality is basically the same as `ibm_cloud`. The new value, `ibm_quantum_platform`, was added as a new channel. The output is the next one:

```python
# Current usage with ServerlessClient
serverless = ServerlessClient(
    host="http://localhost:8000",
    channel="ibm_quantum",
    token="YOUR_IQP_TOKEN"
)

# Future usage of ServerlessClient
serverless = ServerlessClient(
    host="http://localhost:8000",
    channel="ibm_quantum_platform", # "ibm_cloud" value will work the same until its deprecation
    instance="YOUR_CRN_INSTANCE",
    token="YOUR_API_TOKEN"
)

# Current usage with IBMServerlessClient
serverless = IBMServerlessClient(
    channel="ibm_quantum",
    token="YOUR_IQP_TOKEN"
)

# Future usage of IBMServerlessClient
serverless = IBMServerlessClient(
    channel="ibm_quantum_platform", # "ibm_cloud" value will work the same until its deprecation
    instance="YOUR_CRN_INSTANCE",
    token="YOUR_API_TOKEN"
)
```

- Support in the API:
  - IBM Cloud value was change by IBM Quantum Platform
  - Quantum Platform was changed to IBM Quantum
  - IBM Cloud was changed to IBM Quantum Platform

Naming was adapted to reflect the changes in the API. Partners will start receiving `ibm_quantum_platform` as environment variable in their Functions instead of `ibm_cloud`.

body:
This adds a new section to the visible light metalens where we use local field projection and adjoint to fine tune the power directed to the focal spot.

We get a 17% improvement over 15 iterations.

NOTES:

* uses `yaugenst-flex/polyslab-grads` frontend branch, which has not been merged. without the code from this branch, the results will be terrible because the gradients are inaccurate.
* uses local gradient calculation to make use of the changes in this branch. Ideally we would switch to remote gradient.
* The gradient processing takes >5 minutes each iteration.. so I limited the code to only run one iteration. I left the cell output to correspond to the full 15 iterations that I ran locally, along with a small note.

Not sure when is the best time to merge this, maybe after Yannick's PR is merged and it is fast enough to justify running this?

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds a new feature to track and visualize lines of code changed per PR in the GitHub Actions step summary.

## What's Added

**New PR Analysis Features:**
- Tracks lines of code additions, deletions, and total changes per PR
- Counts number of files modified per PR
- Collects data for all PRs (not just Copilot-assisted ones)

**New Chart Visualization:**
- "Lines of Code Changed per PR" chart showing min/avg/max statistics by week
- Detailed data table with additions, deletions, and file counts
- Follows existing chart patterns and styling

## Implementation Details

**PR Analyzer (`src/pr-analyzer.js`):**
- Added `getPRFiles()` method to fetch file changes from GitHub API
- Added `analyzeLineChanges()` method to calculate line statistics
- Integrated line changes tracking into main analysis flow
- Added `lineChanges` field to PR details structure

**Chart Generator (`src/mermaid-generator.js`):**
- Added `calculateLineChangesStatsPerWeek()` for weekly statistics
- Added `generateLineChangesChart()` for mermaid line chart
- Added `generateLineChangesDataTable()` for detailed data table
- Integrated new chart into step summary after existing charts

**Testing:**
- Added comprehensive test coverage for all new functions
- Tests cover normal cases, edge cases, and empty data scenarios
- All existing tests continue to pass (27 total tests)

## Example Output

The new chart appears in GitHub Actions step summary showing:

```mermaid
xychart-beta
    title "Lines of Code Changed per PR by Week"
    x-axis ["24/01", "24/02"]
    y-axis "Lines of Code" 0 --> 190
    line "Min Lines Changed" [40, 30]
    line "Avg Lines Changed" [83.3, 85]
    line "Max Lines Changed" [140, 140]
```

With collapsible detailed data table showing exact statistics for additions, deletions, and files changed.

## Impact

- Provides valuable insights into code change patterns
- Helps identify weeks with significant development activity
- Complements existing PR and commit statistics
- No breaking changes to existing functionality

Fixes #54.

author: d-netto
body:
This used to be an environment variable (`JULIA_GC_NO_GENERATIONAL`) that could only be enabled if Julia was built with `WITH_GC_DEBUG_ENV`.

People benchmarking GC may want to disable generational behavior in non-debug builds as well.

This PR introduces `gc-sweep-always-full` as a hidden command-line-option.

It also moves the docstrings for `--hard-heap-limit` and `--heap-target-increment` into `opts_hidden`, as it should have been done in the original PR.

author: victorstankov
body:
This pull request updates the login functionality to use a POST request with a JSON payload instead of a GET request with query parameters. It includes changes to both the backend and frontend to support this improvement.

### Backend changes:
* **Changed HTTP method for login route**: Updated the `/login` route in `endpoints/authentication.py` to use the POST method instead of GET.
* **Switched to JSON payload for login**: Modified the `login` function to parse JSON from the request body instead of relying on query parameters.
* **Improved error handling**: Replaced the direct return of validation error messages with a generic error message for better security and user experience.
* **Removed unused import**: Removed `make_response` from imports in `endpoints/authentication.py` as it is no longer used.

### Frontend changes:
* **Updated login request format**: Changed the `fetch` call in `frontend/src/routes/Login.jsx` to send login credentials as a JSON object in the request body, along with appropriate headers.

Resolves VST-28

####  **PR extends the test coverage for seven tensor operators in the cTensor library. Overall Test Currently Available, and a Macro approach to Handle Tensor reduce dimension in Tensor_mean and Tensor_sum similar to Pytorch.**
 
**1. Add Operator (test_add.c)**

Category:

- Scalar Addition (1x1 tensors)
- Vector Addition (1D tensors)
- Matrix Addition (2D tensors)
- Broadcasting: vector + scalar-like tensor
- Higher Dimensional Tensors:
  - 3D tensor addition
  - 4D tensor addition
- Gradient Propagation:
   - requires_grad flag propagation

**2. Mul Operator (test_mul.c)**

Category: 

- Scalar Multiplication (1x1 tensors)
- Vector Element-wise Multiplication (1D tensors)
- Matrix Element-wise Multiplication (2D tensors)
- Broadcasting: matrix * scalar-like tensor
- Sign Preservation:
  - Negative number multiplication
- Higher Dimensional Tensors:
  - 3D tensor multiplication

**3. Sub Operator (test_sub.c)**

Category: 

- Scalar Subtraction (1x1 tensors)
- Vector Element-wise Subtraction (1D tensors)
- Matrix Element-wise Subtraction (2D tensors)
- Broadcasting: matrix - scalar-like tensor
- Order Dependency:
  - Verifying a - b ≠ b - a
- Higher Dimensional Tensors:
  - 3D tensor subtraction

**4. Mean Operator (test_mean.c)**

Category: 

- Scalar Mean (1x1 tensors)
- Vector Mean (1D tensors)
- Matrix Mean (2x2 tensors)
- Negative Numbers:
  - Mean of a matrix with negative values
- Zero Values:
  - Mean of a tensor with all zeros
- Large Tensor Reductions:
  - Mean over 1,000 elements
  - Mean over 5,000 elements
- Higher Dimensional Tensors:
  - 3D tensor mean
  - 4D tensor mean
- Edge Cases:
  - Single element mean

**5. MatMul Operator (test_matmul.c)**

Category

- Square Matrix Multiplication (2x2 * 2x2)
- Rectangular Matrix Multiplication (2x3 * 3x2)
- Matrix-Vector Operations:
  - Matrix-Vector (2x2 * 2x1)
  - Vector-Matrix (1x2 * 2x2)
- Edge Matrix Sizes:
  - 1x1 matrix multiplication
  - 3x5 * 5x2 multiplication
- Large Matrix Operations:
  - Stress test with 10x10 matrices
  - Large rectangular (20x15 * 15x25)
- Special Matrix Content:
  - Matrices with zeros

**6. Mulf Operator (test_mulf.c)**

Category

- Scalar Tensor * Float
- Vector Tensor * Float
- Matrix Tensor * Float
- Tensor * Zero
- Special Scalar Values:
  - Multiplication by zero
  - Very small scalar multiplication
- Higher Dimensional Tensors:
  - 3D tensor scalar multiplication
  - 4D tensor scalar multiplication

**7. Sum Operator (test_sum.c)**

Category

- Sum of a scalar tensor
- Sum of a vector tensor
- Sum of a matrix tensor
- Sum of tensor with negative numbers
- Large Tensor Reductions:
  - Sum of 1,000 elements
  - Sum of 5,000 elements
- Higher Dimensional Tensors:
  - 3D tensor sum
  - 4D tensor sum


### Future Improvements
- Broadcasting is not perfectly implemented; that is why there are some problems in the test cases, so it is **commented** and marked as `TODO `for later reference.

This commit introduces two main enhancements:

1.  Folder Upload Functionality:
    - You can now click the "Add Folder" button to open a system dialog and select a folder for processing.
    - Selected files within the folder are read, their SHA-256 hashes are calculated, and they are added to the `fileLog`.
    - The application state (localStorage, file counts, log size) is updated accordingly.
    - Newly added files are displayed in the "Activity" log.
    - Duplicate files (based on path) are not added if already monitored.

2.  Gear Icon Update:
    - The gear icon in the settings panel now behaves more like a button, with the cursor changing to a pointer on hover. This was achieved by adding the `cursor-pointer` class to its container.

The changes include modifications to `index.html` to add the file input and update the gear icon's class, and significant additions to `script.js` to handle the folder selection, file processing logic, and UI updates.

author: vinnybod
body:
This change adds “exclusions” to pom files in two different ways. The results of which are combined for the generated pom.xml.

**per java_export target**

This is useful for when an exclusion is required for a target that is built within the repo.

```python
java_export(
  name="my_dep",
  ...
  maven_coordinates="com.example:my_dep",
  deps=["log4j:log4j"]
)

java_export(
  name="my_lib",
  ...
  maven_coordinates="com.example:my_lib"
  exclusions={
    ":my_dep": ["log4j:log4j"]
  }
)
```

**maven.artifact declarations**

Passes through exclusions defined by the user on the `maven.artifact` to the lock file, which then appear on the generated pom.xml.

```python
# bzlmod
maven.artifact(
    artifact = "guava",
    exclusions = ["com.google.errorprone:error_prone_annotations"],
    group = "com.google.guava",
    version = "31.1-jre",
)

# WORKSPACE
maven_install(
    name = "pom_exclusions_testing",
    artifacts = [
        maven.artifact(
            artifact = "guava",
            exclusions = [
                maven.exclusion(
                    artifact = "error_prone_annotations",
                    group = "com.google.errorprone",
                ),
            ],
            group = "com.google.guava",
            version = "31.1-jre",
        ),
    ],
)
```

Exclusions set by `excluded_artifacts` are not passed along to the `pom.xml`.

----

Some decisions that we discussed but am still open to discussing:

* Does it make to propagate the `excluded_artifacts`?
We decided no on this because it seems like the wrong thing to do. If I for example add `excluded_artifacts=["log4j:log4j"]`, I want to completely exclude it from being brought into my repo via the coursier resolver. But that doesn't necessarily mean I want to add this exclusing to **every single** dependency entry in the pom.xml.

* Is it okay that we essentially ignore how Coursier outputs its exclusions?
I think yes. The current codebase wasn't doing anything with that information at that point. You can see in the new generated lockfiles, all that's changed is a new `exclusions` section.

author: c-prather
body:
Releasing to reflect what the people^TM are using, and to free the `dev` branch up to land Parthenon updates and other disruptive stuff soon.

By far the most notable addition is the inverter recovery #137.  This attempts to set reasonable velocities when floors must be applied to the robust inverter's results. Previously these floors would add to the mass and internal energy while maintaining unrealistic high velocities, causing unphysical heating when the high-velocity zones thermalized during subsequent steps.

Accordingly, some defaults have been changed for better robustness *and* accuracy: better conserving energy and momentum also keeps the simulation stable by preventing positive feedback loops.  Full choices and rationale will be in either the KHARMA paper or a circulated addendum on floors.

This release also adds restarting from phdf files.  You need to specify some extra parameters, see the wiki.

Finally, we'll be landing ISMR here before release, once I have some data on how and whether it helps in different situations.

author: jimdelois
body:
As per the JUCE documentation, the `findChildFiles` method [does not guarantee that the files will be returned in a consistent order](https://docs.juce.com/master/classFile.html#a5290046f7f78fffce0c4debd6668cbe5).  Because of this, the current behavior of downstream clients is such that the files loaded into the layout shortcuts for `CMD + 1`, `CMD + 2`, etc (e.g. on Mac), will actually be tied to a random layout.  This defeats the point of having a "shortcut" at all, given that it is entirely possible that it will change on application reload.

This PR brings a deterministic ordering to the Layout shortcuts by adding a quick `sort` call on the names of the layout files.  A user can then use the filenames, themselves, to coerce desired layouts to specific shortcut keys.

author: goldencaesar
body:
This commit overhauls the folder upload and file scanning functionality in the GoldHash project to address the issue where uploaded files were immediately scanned and added to the activity log.

The new behavior is as follows:

1.  Folder Upload:
    *   When you select a folder to upload, its structure is captured
        and displayed in the sidebar.
    *   Files within the uploaded folder are listed in the "Documents" tab
        when the folder is selected, with an initial status of
        "Not Scanned Yet".
    *   No hashing or logging occurs at the point of upload; the
        "Activity" tab is not affected.
    *   A new data structure, `userUploadedFolders`, is introduced to
        manage these folders you provide separately from demo data until
        they are scanned.

2.  Sidebar and Documents Tab:
    *   The sidebar rendering logic (`updateSidebarView`, `createSidebarEntry`)
        has been generalized to display both demo folders and folders you upload.
    *   The "Documents" tab (`displayFolderContents`) now correctly sources
        file information from either `demoFilesData` or `userUploadedFolders`,
        displaying the appropriate status.

3.  Scanning Process:
    *   The "Scan" button now triggers the `scanFiles` function, which has
        been updated to:
        *   Collect all files from both `demoFilesData` and all
          `userUploadedFolders`.
        *   Read the content of files you uploaded (which were previously
          only referenced by their `File` objects).
        *   Perform SHA-256 hashing.
        *   Update the global `fileLog` with appropriate statuses
          ('newly_added', 'modified', 'verified').
        *   Refresh both the "Activity" tab and the "Documents" tab to
          reflect the scan results.

This change provides a more intuitive experience by giving you explicit control over when file scanning occurs and clearly separating the action of adding a folder for monitoring from the action of scanning its contents.

author: riccardomc
body:
## Problem Statement

This pull request implements the suggestion in #2987 which allows to merge secret values from different secrets obtained from a provider through a `dataFrom.find` in one single `Secret` according to configurable priority, merge strategy and conflict policy.

## Related Issue

Implements #2987 

## Proposed Changes

The implementation extends the `ExternalSecretDataFromRemoteRef` API by introducing a new `ExternalSecretRewriteMerge` method to instruct the controller on how to perform merge operations on secret key/value pairs as part of `ExternalSecretRewrite`.

The implementation follows [this](https://github.com/external-secrets/external-secrets/issues/2987#issuecomment-1876042314) detailed suggestion comment for the most part, with some interpretations and choices.

```yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: example
spec:
  # ...
  dataFrom:
  - find:
      path: cluster1/backend
      name: 
        regexp: ".*"
    rewrite:
    - merge:
        # define the key under which we want to store the resulting merged values
        # It is required if the strategy is 'JSON' and ignored if strategy is 'Extract' 
        into: ""

        # JSON: keep the keys (secret names from the provider)
        # and only merge the secret values, treating it as JSON.
        # The resulting JSON object is stored in the `into` property.
        #
        # Extract: parse the value as JSON and hoist
        # the key/value pairs up just like dataFrom.Extract it does.
        strategy: Extract # or JSON

        # Control the behavior when a conflicting key/value is encountered
        # When conflictPolicy=Ignore the conflicting key/value will be 
        # silently overridden. When conflictPolicy=Error the conflict will cause
        # an Error that will be reported in the Status of the ExternalSecret with
        # details about all conflicting keys.
        conflictPolicy: Error # or Ignore

        # define a list of keys that take precedence over all keys,
        # no matter what sorting strategy/order is being used.
        # These priority-keys are merged into the result map
        # in the defined order.
        priority:
          - custom-stuff-controlled-by-developers
``` 

Found secret keys are sorted in alphabetical order before being processed. This guarantees a stable and predictable conflict resolution order. Keys specified in the `priority` list are processed after all the others, guaranteeing that the last key on the `priority` list has precedence over all the others. 

Documentation and extensive unit tests are provided to further illustrate the implementation details.

The diff looks pretty big, but its conceptually pretty simple. The interface for multiple targets just needs an additional argument for the predicted `X` data / covariates.  I tried to make everything as consistent as possible with the existing functions and to `@njit` as much as possible.

Most of the changes are just refactoring to reuse code across the different model families. I hope this makes it easier to add additional GLM families soon. You need to specify functions for initialization, loss, gradient, and statistics. The `get_stats` function can be constructed out of functions for pointwise (what I called "scalar" in the code; not sure what term you'd call this) gradient and hessian, as well as the link.   

I added tests similar to what was there before. Notably, these tests don't test weighting or the `lam` or `coord` parameters.

I started a few improvements that aren't consistent across the code base:

I added type hints to the functions I introduced. It would be nice to do this at least for the rest of the public functions, but I'm putting off making additional changes until I get some feedback on this proposal.

I made some of the tests deterministic to avoid random failures.

Looking forward to your feedback and response!

author: dmitrykos
body:
Improves Dynamic Range (DR) of converters.

Currently, at this stage, DR of 8-bit is improved. For example Float32 to 8-bit converters got around 8+ dB DR improvement:

```c
=== Combined dynamic range (src->dest->float32) ===
Key: Noise amplitude in dBfs, X - fail (either above failed or dest->float32 failed)
{{{
in|  out:      f32     i32     i24     i16      i8     ui8
 f32          -inf  -180.6  -138.5   -79.5   -39.5   -39.4
 i32        -144.5  -144.5     X     -85.9   -40.1   -39.4
 i24        -138.5  -138.5  -138.5   -86.1   -39.4   -39.5
 i16         -84.8   -84.8   -84.8   -84.8   -39.8   -39.7
  i8         -36.6   -36.6   -36.6   -36.6   -36.6   -36.6
 ui8         -36.4   -36.4   -36.4   -36.4   -36.4   -36.4
}}}
```

Dithered variant was improved too by modifying the way the dithered noise is applied. Before we truncated sample by 1 bit to add space for a dither noise. With this approach valid audio data info was truncated and we were getting an explicit dither noise. But, if there is no initial truncation and dither noise is added then we effectively mix all valid audio data with noise first and truncate it afterwards - this approach increases DR by at least 1 dB in case of 8-bit converters (will work similarly for other formats).

New approach on example of `Int32_To_Int8_Dither` converter:
```c
dither = PaUtil_Generate16BitTriangularDither( ditherGenerator );

/* truncate to 24-bit, add dither, truncate resulting 24-bit value to 8-bit */
*dest = (signed char) ((((*src) >> 8) + dither) >> 16);
```

Here we truncate 32-bit sample to 24-bit to add some gap for calculations, add dither and only then truncate to final 8-bits.

I can further extend this PR to other formats and cleanup and re-factor existing code, which in some places is incorrect, in order to get maximum DR for all converters. All implementations will be commented, so that we will no longer have unexplained calculations and conversions. The quality of audio output of PA will definitely improve.

Awaiting comments.

author: lacymorrow
body:
Critical regressions from PR %2318 were addressed with comprehensive fixes.

*   Memory exhaustion was resolved by implementing bounded audio buffers (e.g., `MAX_AUDIO_BUFFER_SIZE`, `MAX_MEMORY_USAGE_MB`) and automatic cleanup mechanisms in `tauri-plugin-voice-transcription/src/always_listening.rs` and `tauri-plugin-voice-transcription/src/controller.rs`. A `MemoryTracker` using `RwLock` was introduced for thread-safe memory monitoring.
*   Threading safety issues and audio pipeline instability were mitigated by enhancing synchronization with `RwLock` in `always_listening.rs` and `controller.rs`, alongside robust error handling and resource management in audio stream processing.
*   Linux compilation failures were fixed by moving voice-specific dependencies to platform-conditional sections in `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`. Voice plugin initialization in `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` and all voice commands in `src-tauri/src/commands/always_listening.rs` were made conditional, ensuring graceful degradation on unsupported platforms.

These changes restore cross-platform compilation and significantly improve application stability and memory usage.

### What
- This PR updates the cloud console links in Terra to include the `authuser=<user_email>` parameter. Previously, some links were missing, causing issues for users who had multiple Google accounts.

- Without the authuser parameter, the browser defaults to the user’s primary Google account, which may not match the one used to log in to Terra. This led to IAM errors and confusion when opening links. Adding `authuser` ensures the correct identity is used consistently.

body:
#### 7b37bf4eada1c881ba0453f9dc6b04b772a03e47 
Allow WKNavigationAction.request.URL to be valid NSURL that isn't valid WTF::URL
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=294333
rdar://145790356

Reviewed by Chris Dumez.

In 289946@main I made it so an invalid WTF::URL can't convert to a valid NSURL.
This fixed a large number of issues involving improper use of URLs.
However, this also prevented a legitimate use of invalid WTF::URLs:
An app can get a WKNavigationAction with the URL and decide to do something with
it that is not related to WebKit.  For compatibility, we need to explicitly allow
this.  Since the WebCore::ResourceRequest IPC encoder uses conversion to NSURL,
if we have an invalid WTF::URL we need to send the invalid URL string separately
then use it on the other side.  Since NSURL.URLWithString also doesn't successfully
parse such a URL, we need to use CFURLCreateAbsoluteURLWithBytes, which I made
into its own function to share between its existing and introduced uses.

An alternative I considered was to percent encode spaces in hosts of URLs with
non-special schemes, but that goes against behavior of Chrome, Firefox, Safari,
and NSURL.URLWithString so I decided not to.

# Pull Request: [STI-43] 3D View for Wheel Spacers

## Related Tickets & US
- [STI-88] 3D View for Wheel Spacers - https://linear.app/stic/issue/STI-43/vista-3d-de-separadores-de-aro

## Description

This PR implements the interactive 3D visualization of wheel spacers, allowing users to view and examine the details of the spacer (e.g., diameter, PCD, material, thickness) before proceeding with the quotation or purchase.

- The 3D view allows the user to rotate, zoom, and pan the spacer.
- The view is updated based on the user’s specifications (diameter, PCD, material, thickness).
- The 3D visualization is smooth and responsive, even with complex models.
- The user can switch between different types of spacers and visualize how the 3D model changes.
- Integrated with the quotation system to update the 3D view as the user selects different options (e.g., material, size).

## What did I Do?

- Implemented a 3D interactive view using [Three.js, Babylon.js, or another 3D library].
- Created a `WheelSpacer3DView` component that:
  - Displays a 3D model of the spacer
  - Supports interactions such as rotate, zoom, and pan
- Integrated the 3D model with the wheel spacer quotation system:
  - The 3D model updates based on user-selected specifications (e.g., diameter, material, thickness)
- Ensured the visualization is fluid and responsive, even with complex models
- Implemented the ability to change between different types of spacers and view the corresponding 3D model
- Enhanced the UI for seamless interaction with the 3D view

## How to Test

1. Navigate to the wheel spacer quotation page in the system.

author: wade-arista
body:
Use the go-retryablehttp client with its default retry policy to retry on server errors.

This will avoid bazeldnf killing bazel builds unnecessarily in the case of temporary downstream service errors.

body:
Azure is retiring basic sku for load balancers and public IPs, which were the default options for these clusters when they are created, unfortunately this isn't as simple as changing a sku value, and although the original author of the deployment templates have the standard sku option for the clusters, they are also outdated with the latest changes to the standard load balancer.

- Change public IP\load balancer to use standard sku
- disableOutboundSnat needs to be set explicitly in the external load balancing rules since we now use outbound rules to manage this
- Add NAT gateway on the existing es subnet (the deployment scripts will try to create public IPs for the client nodes if standard sku load balancers are chosen, this *could be an option previously but outbound rules for standard load balancers (released in 2024) do not allow backend pools to have individual public IPs; this forces us to use NAT gateway instead
- Remove all references and creation of public IPs for master\client\data nodes, kibana and jumpbox nodes are excluded from since they don't use the shared vm template

author: e40pud
body:
## Summary

Main ticket ([Internal link](https://github.com/elastic/security-team/issues/12790))

With these changes we add attack discovery alerts deduplication. Right now identical attack are being stored within the alerts index and to filter duplicates out we will use the next approach:

1. Each alert will have a ID generated as a SHA256 of attack attributes: list of SIEM `alerts IDs`, `connector ID`, `owner ID` (`username`/`profile_uid` for ad hoc logic and `scheduleId` in case of schedules) and `space ID`
2. After LLM generates attack discoveries we would check whether the attack alert with the ID that describes the attack based on the rule above exists in the alerts index
3. If such an alerts exists we would drop the generated discovery
4. Otherwise, we would proceed with storing the attack discovery as a new alert

## NOTES

The feature is hidden behind the feature flag (in `kibana.dev.yml`):

```
feature_flags.overrides:
  securitySolution.attackDiscoveryAlertsEnabled: true
```

body:
### TL;DR

Added chat message management functionality including retrieving messages, deleting chats, and automatic chat title generation.

### What changed?

- Added `getChatMessages` query to fetch messages for a specific chat
- Implemented `deleteChat` mutation to remove chats and their associated messages
- Added `deleteMessage` internal mutation
- Removed the need to pass `userId` explicitly in `generateUserMessage` by extracting it from the session
- Enhanced the sidebar to include delete buttons for chats
- Added automatic chat title generation based on the first message
- Updated the chat view to load existing messages when viewing a chat
- Created a new API endpoint `/api/generateChatTitle` that uses AI to create relevant chat titles

### How to test?

1. Create a new chat and verify that it gets an automatically generated title
2. View an existing chat and confirm that all messages load correctly
3. Delete a chat from the sidebar and verify that it's removed along with its messages
4. Send messages in a chat and verify they're properly associated with the current user

### Why make this change?

These changes improve the user experience by providing better chat management capabilities. Users can now view message history, delete unwanted chats, and get meaningful chat titles automatically. The code is also more secure by deriving the user ID from the session rather than passing it explicitly.

author: banteg
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a SQL syntax error in the `zksynclite_swaps` table definition where `TEXT_NOT NULL` should be `TEXT NOT NULL`.

## Changes

1. **Fixed SQL syntax in schema.py**: Changed `TEXT_NOT NULL` to `TEXT NOT NULL` in the `to_amount` column definition
2. **Added database upgrade v48→v49**: Created upgrade script to fix existing databases
   - Checks if the table exists and has the bug
   - Creates a new table with correct schema
   - Migrates data (converting any NULL values to '0' as a safety measure)
   - Drops old table and renames the new one
3. **Regenerated minimized schemas**: Updated to reflect the corrected syntax

## Testing

The upgrade handles edge cases:
- Skips if table doesn't exist
- Skips if table already has correct schema
- Safely converts any NULL values to '0' (though they shouldn't exist)

## Related Issues

Fixes SQL syntax bug discovered during code review.

body:
Thanks for assigning this issue to me. I'm starting to work on it and will keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.

Original issue description:

> ## Problem
> 
> The current Settings page (`app/settings.tsx`) only has a stub for subscription cancellation and does not allow the user to sign out.
> 
> ## Proposal
> At minimum, the Settings page should provide:
> - A working option to cancel or manage the user's subscription (if user is subscribed, allow cancellation/downgrade; if not, hide or disable)
> - An option for the user to sign out (including handling both authenticated and anonymous sessions)
> 
> This aligns with common user expectations and the current app features (Stripe integration and documented sign out workflows).
> 
> ## Acceptance Criteria
> - [ ] Users can cancel or manage their current subscription from the Settings page
> - [ ] Users can sign out from the Settings page
> - [ ] Both actions provide user feedback and handle errors gracefully
> 


Fixes #325.
